title: A Protocol for the Echo
premise: Astrid Lockridge smuggles forbidden memories between the two halves of humanity that split after the Sundering: the orbital Consensus and the cryo-ark fleet Meridian. When his ship intercepts a distress call in a dead language, he discovers the arks' sleepers are dying and only a memory-smuggler's neural rig can carry the waking protocol between worlds. To save them he must ally with Sefa, a Consensus auditor sent to arrest him, and choose which half of humanity wakes first — knowing the other half will not survive the delay. In the end Astrid splits himself across both fleets, uploading half his mind to each, so that no one wakes alone and everyone wakes diminished.
about_author: Mirabel Crane is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent nine years relaying messages between ships that never met. She writes about distance, duty, and the people who refuse to let either have the last word.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Mind
chapters.summary: Astrid runs a hold full of illegal memories past orbital customs at Vesper Gate, narrating with wry detachment. A near-miss inspection reveals how much of his own past he's sold away. Beat: competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. He takes the smuggling run between the silent halves of humanity, delivering a dying grandmother's memories to kin on ark Meridian. The grief of his clients underscores what the Sundering cost. Beat: tenderness in transaction.

chapters.title: Signal in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: His rig decodes a distress broadcast in Pre-Sundering English, extinct for two centuries. The signal originates from inside the ark fleet itself. Beat: dread and irresistible curiosity.

chapters.title: Customs Auditor
chapters.summary: Sefa Ilyes, POV introduced. A Consensus auditor hunting memory-smugglers, she traces the same anomalous signal and realizes her government already knows — and is lying. Beat: duty beginning to crack.

chapters.title: Boarding Party
chapters.summary: Sefa catches Astrid at Vesper Gate but finds his decoded signal matches classified files on her own terminal. She lets him go, officially 'losing' him. Beat: complicity as attraction.

chapters.title: What the Arks Dream
chapters.summary: Astrid docks with ark Meridian under false papers. Cryo-bays are failing; sleepers show neural decay. An old engineer, Dagny, confirms the distress call is real and two centuries old. Beat: horror in slow motion.

chapters.title: Two Hundred Years Late
chapters.summary: Dagny's POV flashback chapter: the arks' waking protocol was deliberately withheld by the Consensus at the Sundering. The sleepers were hostages all along. Beat: righteous fury.

chapters.title: The Price of Passage
chapters.summary: Astrid learns the waking protocol requires a human neural bridge — one mind must carry it intact between fleets. His rig makes him the only candidate alive. Beat: the trap closing.

chapters.title: Auditor's Doubt
chapters.summary: Sefa interrogates her superiors and is fed a cover story about plague aboard the arks. She doesn't believe it. Beat: loyalty inverted.

chapters.title: Dead Drop
chapters.summary: Astrid and Sefa meet covertly, each pretending they haven't chosen sides. They trade information like contraband. Beat: intimacy through espionage.

chapters.title: Meridian's Children
chapters.summary: Born awake aboard the arks, a generation raised as caretakers of sleeping ancestors. Young tech Joon shows Astrid the nursery bays. Beat: inherited grief.

chapters.title: The Consensus Decides
chapters.summary: Consensus council POV: they vote to let the arks fail rather than risk the waking protocol empowering the fleet. Sefa's mentor votes yes. Beat: cold institutional math.

chapters.title: Run the Gap
chapters.summary: Astrid attempts to copy the protocol from a derelict relay station in the inter-fleet gap; Sefa covers his approach from customs. A patrol nearly kills them both. Beat: adrenaline and trust.

chapters.title: Half a Memory
chapters.summary: Testing the transfer, Astrid discovers carrying the protocol will overwrite part of his mind — permanently. He hides this from Sefa. Beat: quiet self-sacrifice seeded.

chapters.title: Joon's Choice
chapters.summary: Joon, desperate, tries to wake his mother early and destroys a cryo-bay. The crew turns on Dagny's faction. Beat: good intentions as sabotage.

chapters.title: Warrant for One Smuggler
chapters.summary: Sefa is ordered to arrest Astrid or be arrested herself. She burns her career instead, sending him warning. Beat: love against duty, first open breach.

chapters.title: Fugitives Together
chapters.summary: On the run in the gap, Astrid and Sefa stop performing. A night of honesty — and closeness — between two people trained to surveil. Beat: found family begins with two.

chapters.title: The Second Signal
chapters.summary: A second distress call, newer, reveals the arks aren't the only dying party: the Consensus's orbital habitats are failing too, dependent on ark-built infrastructure. Both halves are sinking. Beat: the binary collapses.

chapters.title: Dagny's Ledger
chapters.summary: Dagny reveals the arks' founders anticipated betrayal and hid a second protocol fragment — split between the fleets by design, forcing cooperation. Beat: hope with a price tag.

chapters.title: Council of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Sefa confronts her mentor with the habitat data. He admits everything and asks her to stay silent for stability's sake. She refuses. Beat: severance from the old family.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Consensus warships move to seize Meridian before any waking can occur. Astrid's ship is caught in the net; Dagny dies covering the escape. Beat: first major loss.

chapters.title: Grief Cargo
chapters.summary: Astrid carries Dagny's final memories as cargo, unable to jettison them. Joon blames him. The found family fractures. Beat: guilt as ballast.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of Waking
chapters.summary: Hard numbers: power and protocol capacity mean only half the combined population can wake within the window. Someone must choose. Beat: the central dilemma sharpened.

chapters.title: Vote Among Thieves
chapters.summary: Astrid convenes smugglers, ark-born, and defector auditors — his strange new family — to decide who wakes. They deadlock. Beat: democracy's cruelty.

chapters.title: Sefa's Answer
chapters.summary: Sefa proposes splitting the protocol so both fleets wake partially, staggered over years. It requires a mind stable enough to hold both halves: Astrid's. Beat: love demanding sacrifice.

chapters.title: He Refuses
chapters.summary: Astrid refuses and plans to run the whole protocol to the arks alone, dooming the orbitals. Sefa calls it cowardice dressed as mercy. Beat: lovers at war.

chapters.title: The Empty Bay
chapters.summary: Astrid visits the cryo-bay where his own sister has slept for sixty years, unfindable among forty thousand. He never told Sefa why he runs this route. Beat: motive revealed.

chapters.title: Joon's Forgiveness
chapters.summary: Joon finds his mother's decayed pattern beyond saving and finally understands the arithmetic. He reconciles with Astrid and joins the staggered-waking plan. Beat: grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Countdown at Vesper Gate
chapters.summary: The window closes in seventy-two hours. Warships mass. The smuggler fleet volunteers as decoys — the found family risking everything for strangers. Beat: solidarity as climax approach.

chapters.title: The Bridge Run
chapters.summary: Astrid begins the neural load, the protocol burning through his memories street by street, face by face. Sefa anchors him with her voice. Beat: sacrifice made intimate.

chapters.title: What He Forgets First
chapters.summary: Mid-transfer, Astrid loses his childhood, then his sister's face. He keeps going, choosing strangers over self. Beat: the price paid in real time.

chapters.title: Warships at the Gate
chapters.summary: The Consensus attacks as the transfer completes. Sefa broadcasts the habitat failure data fleet-wide, turning crews against their orders. Beat: truth as weapon.

chapters.title: Mutiny of Auditors
chapters.summary: Customs officers, Sefa's former colleagues, refuse the assault. Her mentor stands down the fleet at gunpoint of public opinion. Beat: institutions bending to people.

chapters.title: Split
chapters.summary: The transfer finishes: half of Astrid's mind lives in each fleet's waking system. Both populations begin to wake — diminished, staggered, alive. Beat: triumph braided with loss.

chapters.title: The Man in Two Places
chapters.summary: Both halves of Astrid wake in medical bays, each missing the other without knowing why. Sefa travels between them. Beat: love persisting past wholeness.

chapters.title: Waking Meridian
chapters.summary: Ark sleepers rise to a world that kept faith badly but kept faith. Joon greets the first wakened children. Beat: earned grace.

chapters.title: Waking the Orbitals
chapters.summary: Habitat evacuees resettle as the fleets formally end the Sundering. The first joint census counts everyone twice, once per half of Astrid. Beat: reconciliation without erasure.

chapters.title: Echo Protocol
chapters.summary: The two halves of Astrid begin exchanging memories across the new link, slowly reassembling. Some gaps never close. Sefa decides she loves the sum anyway. Beat: acceptance.

chapters.title: A Protocol for the Echo
chapters.summary: Years later, the waking protocol becomes standard law: no colony sleeps alone, no message goes unanswered. Astrid — both of him — teaches smugglers-turned-liaisons. Beat: legacy.

chapters.title: The Long Route Home
chapters.summary: Final chapter, alternating between both Astrids meeting at last in the middle of the gap where Dagny died. They complete each other's sentences, missing the same words. Sefa waits at either end. Beat: peace, imperfect and chosen.
